Meets 100% of demonstrated need for undergraduates
CSS Profile + FAFSA required for institutional aid; priority deadlines Nov 3 (ED) and Feb 1 (RD) (dates from the aid site's current-year page)

$103,180-$103,975 first-year COA 2026-27 (tuition $73,740; fees $3,019; housing $11,560; food $10,469; books $536; personal $3,274; travel $582-1,318; Pratt dues $60)
Early Decision (binding) due Nov 2, decisions mid-December; Regular Decision due Jan 4. No EA. ED admits may be released for financial reasons in some cases

Optional alumni interviews (virtual), offered by invitation only, prioritized where more information is needed; cannot be requested; not being offered one doesn't hurt. Optional Glimpse video (U.S. schools). CDS C7: 'Considered'
Apply to either Trinity College of Arts & Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering; Pratt applicants need calculus (physics strongly recommended)

supplements.label: Why Duke
supplements.prompt: What is your impression of Duke as a university and community, and why do you believe it is a good match for your goals, values, and interests? If there is something specific that attracts you to our academic offerings in Trinity College of Arts and Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering, or to our co-curricular opportunities, feel free to include that, too.

supplements.label: Communities
supplements.prompt: We all belong to communities defined by place, faith, family, culture, interests, or shared experience. Tell us about a community that has shaped who you are, any way it has set you apart, and what you’ve learned from being part of it that you hope to bring to Duke.

supplements.label: Optional (choose one): Viewpoints and Experiences
supplements.prompt: We believe a wide range of viewpoints and experiences is essential to maintaining Duke’s vibrant living and learning community. Please share anything in this context that might help us better understand you and your potential contributions to Duke.

supplements.label: Optional (choose one): Difference of Opinion
supplements.prompt: Meaningful dialogue often involves respectful disagreement. Provide an example of a difference of opinion you’ve had with someone you care about. What did you learn from it?

supplements.label: Optional (choose one): Something You Are Excited About
supplements.prompt: What’s the last thing that you’ve been really excited about?
